findings.title: Standalone launch leaves the fixed review range unresolved
findings.claim: codex-review.md shipped literal placeholders; the documented launch piped the file raw, so the reviewer got no range.
findings.how: Inspected the launch block: it performed no substitution. This session's review only worked because the range was supplied out of band.
findings.disposition: FIXED — scripts/launch-review.sh resolves repo/base/target, builds both worktrees, refuses non-existent commits. Acceptance test (zero unresolved placeholders) FAILED on first attempt and drove removing the placeholder block at source.

findings.title: Read-only enforcement makes independent validation impossible
findings.claim: The reviewer owns test verification but the sandbox cannot run either suite.
findings.how: Reviewer's own trace: pytest died before collection with no writable temp dir; detached worktree has no node_modules.
findings.disposition: FIXED — AGENTS.md 8.2 makes SKIPPED_ENVIRONMENT the honest default and documents a disposable-clone mode with 'git status --short' clean as acceptance.

findings.title: Default Playwright validation accesses production
findings.claim: playwright.config.ts falls back to the production Railway URL when SUGGESTER_BACKEND_URL is unset.
findings.how: Read playwright.config.ts:7-8 directly; confirmed the fallback and that webServer.env propagates it.
findings.disposition: DOCUMENTED in both repos with an explicit override; config default deliberately NOT changed — deferred to Son.
findings.note: PARTIAL DISAGREEMENT: reviewer graded this a breach of AGENTS.md 3 'no production access by default'. That section enumerates WRITE operations; these are read-only GETs against a public endpoint. The remedy is still worth doing for evidence stability, so the disagreement changes the rationale, not the action.

findings.title: Claude session prompt both requires and forbids pushing
findings.claim: claude-session-1.md ordered a push in step 6 and forbade one in its safety section and closing line.
findings.how: Read the three blocks together; the implementer had independently hit this and escalated to Son before the review ran.
findings.disposition: FIXED — one conditional rule keyed to whether the reviewer can read local commits.

findings.title: Mandatory remediation record uses the wrong backend-relative path
findings.claim: AGENTS.md and codex-review.md cited backend/research_archive/... which does not exist from the backend root.
findings.how: Compared both paths from the repo root; the prefixed one fails, breaking the mandatory preread.
findings.disposition: FIXED — path corrected in both files.

findings.title: Backend virtualenv described as committed when it is local and ignored
findings.claim: CLAUDE.md called .venv committed; nothing under it is tracked.
findings.disposition: FIXED — described as developer-local, with fresh-checkout bootstrap and the verified cross-worktree interpreter invocation.
findings.note: MECHANISM CORRECTED: reviewer implied .gitignore excludes it. It does not — .gitignore lists 'venv/', which does not match '.venv/'. The venv module writes .venv/.gitignore containing '*', so it self-excludes. Conclusion unchanged, cause different.

findings.title: Frontend cleanup issued from the backend repository
findings.claim: Documented cleanup always cd'd to the backend, which cannot remove the frontend's worktree.
findings.how: The two repos keep separate worktree metadata; confirmed via separate 'git worktree list' outputs.
findings.disposition: FIXED — repository-aware cleanup via git -C, and scripts/launch-review.sh --clean, both exercised.

findings.title: Frontend decision-safety test coverage overstated
findings.claim: Four invariants were credited to one spec; it enforces two.
findings.how: Grepped the specs: empty state lives in contract-deterministic.spec.ts; NO spec asserts the significance-language rule.
findings.disposition: FIXED — enforcement split named per-spec, and the unautomated rule called out as reviewed by eye.

speculative_risks_accepted.disposition: Recorded as an open decision; no vercel.json exists, setting is dashboard-side and unverified.

report.note: Verbatim reviewer report, sections 1-13. The surrounding raw transcript was sandbox noise and is not retained.
report.text:
## 1. Executive verdict

The workflow has strong role separation, fixed Git isolation, WC26 preservation, and real-money safeguards. It is not yet safe to adopt because four P0 defects remain:

- The standalone Codex launch does not supply its promised fixed commit ranges.
- The read-only sandbox cannot execute the prescribed validation.
- Playwright defaults to the production Railway backend.
- The Claude session prompt simultaneously orders and prohibits a push.

No implementation, model, migration, API, deployment configuration, or durable evidence changed.

## 2. Scope and exact commit ranges

Backend:

- Repository: `github.com/SonNguyen2914/TRIVELA`
- Range: `e8c755487940383e7d35b46a964abfd957d04ed8..3201f6f46ba40e734641ec449550ac5ccba30fd9`
- Target descends from base: yes
- Changed: `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `agent-prompts/claude-session-1.md`, `agent-prompts/codex-review.md`

Frontend:

- Repository: `github.com/SonNguyen2914/namson-dev`
- Range: `6833701e5c5e23cf5cfcd61da2ac212a29b9e70d..798ae9c606a81f5b4f735e0f852f35a4699bb822`
- Target descends from base: yes
- Changed: `AGENTS.md`

No local `origin/*` ref contains either target, so `Pushed to origin: no` according to current remote-tracking state. I did not fetch GitHub.

## 3. Repository and worktree state

- Both reviewer worktrees are clean, detached, and fixed at the supplied target commits.
- Backend reviewer: `/private/tmp/trivela-review-backend`
- Frontend reviewer: `/private/tmp/trivela-review-frontend`
- Implementer worktrees are distinct, under `/Users/ns/dev/TRIVELA/{backend,frontend}`.
- Both implementation branches are named `agent-workflow-seed`.
- `~/dev/TRIVELA` is an umbrella directory, not a Git repository.
- Remotes and default branches match the documented repositories and `origin/main`.

## 4. Validation performed

| Check | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Backend range/diff/ancestry | `PASSED_INDEPENDENTLY` | Clean detached target; ancestry confirmed; `git diff --check` clean |
| Frontend range/diff/ancestry | `FAILED_INDEPENDENTLY` | State and ancestry passed, but `git diff --check` reports a new blank line at EOF |
| Backend SQLite pytest | `SKIPPED_ENVIRONMENT` | Attempted; pytest failed before collection because no writable temporary directory exists |
| Backend PostgreSQL pytest | `SKIPPED_ENVIRONMENT` | No verified throwaway PostgreSQL database; sandbox cannot create temp data |
| Alembic upgrade | `SKIPPED_ENVIRONMENT` | No verified throwaway database |
| Frontend TypeScript | `SKIPPED_ENVIRONMENT` | Detached worktree lacks `node_modules`; compiler attempt produced dependency-resolution errors, not product errors |
| Frontend build | `SKIPPED_ENVIRONMENT` | Requires dependencies and writes `.next` under a read-only sandbox |
| Playwright | `SKIPPED_ENVIRONMENT` | Missing dependencies/output access, and the default configuration reaches production |
| Codex CLI claims | `PASSED_INDEPENDENTLY` | Exact version `codex-cli 0.145.0-alpha.30`; `exec -C`, `--sandbox`, and `review --base` exist |
| Claude MCP claim | `PASSED_INDEPENDENTLY` | Claude Code 2.1.220 reports no MCP servers configured |
| V9.5 backend validation | `RELEASE_REPORTED_ONLY` | Remediation record reports 537 backend/PostgreSQL tests and migration round-trips |

The applicable MCP status is `CODEX_INSTALLED_NO_MCP`.

## 5. Confirmed findings by severity

### Finding 1

Title: Standalone launch leaves the fixed review range unresolved  
Severity: HIGH  
Status: CONFIRMED  
Repository: Backend  
File / lines: [agent-prompts/codex-review.md:12–52](/tmp/trivela-review-backend/agent-prompts/codex-review.md:12)  
Evidence: The launch command passes the file unchanged, while its repository, base, and target fields remain literal placeholders. The current session worked only because Son separately supplied both review ranges.  
Reproduction: Inspect lines 12–13 and 42–48; the command performs no substitution or argument injection.  
Impact: A standalone reviewer cannot identify the intended diff without an undocumented second input and is explicitly forbidden from inferring it.  
Recommended correction: Add a wrapper or documented invocation that requires and injects full repository/base/target values for every changed repository.

### Finding 2

Title: Mechanical read-only enforcement makes independent validation impossible  
Severity: HIGH  
Status: CONFIRMED  
Repository: Backend and frontend  
File / lines: [AGENTS.md:235–266](/tmp/trivela-review-backend/AGENTS.md:235), [codex-review.md:12–18](/tmp/trivela-review-backend/agent-prompts/codex-review.md:12)  
Evidence: The sandbox denies writes even under `/tmp`. Pytest could not create its capture temporary file; `tests/conftest.py` also creates a temporary SQLite database. The frontend worktree has no `node_modules`, while `npm install`, TypeScript incremental state, `.next`, and Playwright results all require writes.  
Reproduction: The documented backend interpreter failed before test collection with “No usable temporary directory.” The frontend compiler could not resolve dependencies from the isolated checkout.  
Impact: The reviewer owns command/test verification but cannot independently execute either repository’s principal validation workflow.  
Recommended correction: Keep tracked source immutable while granting a dedicated disposable writable temp/cache/build area, or run the reviewer in an isolated scratch clone where generated artifacts are allowed and verified not to change tracked files.

### Finding 3

Title: Default Playwright validation accesses production  
Severity: HIGH  
Status: CONFIRMED  
Repository: Backend and frontend  
File / lines: [backend AGENTS.md:261–267](/tmp/trivela-review-backend/AGENTS.md:261), [frontend AGENTS.md:63–68](/tmp/trivela-review-frontend/AGENTS.md:63), [playwright.config.ts:7](/tmp/trivela-review-frontend/playwright.config.ts:7)  
Evidence: The canonical command is `npx playwright test`, while the config defaults `SUGGESTER_BACKEND_URL` to the production Railway URL. The frontend rule recommends Playwright because `preview_start` forces production, but Playwright does the same unless explicitly overridden.  
Reproduction: Read `BACKEND` and `webServer.env` in `playwright.config.ts`; no environment override appears in the documented command.  
Impact: Routine reviewer validation violates “no production access by default” and makes volatile live data part of the default evidence.  
Recommended correction: Make hermetic/local data the default Playwright project. Put live-production smoke tests behind an explicit operator-approved opt-in.

### Finding 4

Title: Claude session prompt both requires and forbids pushing  
Severity: HIGH  
Status: CONFIRMED  
Repository: Backend  
File / lines: [agent-prompts/claude-session-1.md:67–110](/tmp/trivela-review-backend/agent-prompts/claude-session-1.md:67)  
Evidence: Lines 67–76 require pushing the implementation branch. Lines 90–92 say “no push,” and line 110 repeats “Do not push.” The prompt also assumes the reviewer is likely cloud-backed, which the final workflow established was false here.  
Reproduction: Read the three cited instruction blocks together.  
Impact: The implementer can either perform an unauthorized outward action or starve a cloud reviewer while still claiming compliance.  
Recommended correction: Replace all three blocks with one conditional rule based on an established local-versus-cloud reviewer result and explicit deployment-branch confirmation.

### Finding 5

Title: Mandatory remediation record uses the wrong backend-relative path  
Severity: MEDIUM  
Status: CONFIRMED  
Repository: Backend  
File / lines: [AGENTS.md:283–294](/tmp/trivela-review-backend/AGENTS.md:283), [codex-review.md:54–59](/tmp/trivela-review-backend/agent-prompts/codex-review.md:54)  
Evidence: From the documented backend working directory, `backend/research_archive/...` does not exist. The file is `research_archive/v95_evaluation_remediation_2026-07-26.json`. My initial mandated read failed on the documented path.  
Reproduction: From the backend root, compare the existence of the two paths.  
Impact: Reviewers can miss the settled-defect record and re-report deliberately deferred items.  
Recommended correction: Use the backend-root-relative path consistently.

### Finding 6

Title: Backend virtualenv is described as committed when it is local and ignored  
Severity: MEDIUM  
Status: CONFIRMED  
Repository: Backend  
File / lines: [CLAUDE.md:21–29](/tmp/trivela-review-backend/CLAUDE.md:21), [AGENTS.md:235–244](/tmp/trivela-review-backend/AGENTS.md:235)  
Evidence: `git ls-files` returns nothing under `.venv`; the detached worktree has no `.venv`; only the developer’s main checkout has one. The two documents contradict each other.  
Reproduction: Run `git ls-files '.venv/**'` and inspect a fresh worktree.  
Impact: A cloud or fresh-clone implementer is told to invoke dependencies that were never committed and receives no bootstrap instructions.  
Recommended correction: Describe `.venv` as developer-local and document the verified bootstrap path when absent.

### Finding 7

Title: Frontend cleanup is issued from the backend repository  
Severity: MEDIUM  
Status: CONFIRMED  
Repository: Backend  
File / lines: [AGENTS.md:207–229](/tmp/trivela-review-backend/AGENTS.md:207)  
Evidence: Creation says “backend or frontend,” but cleanup always changes to `~/dev/TRIVELA/backend`. Backend Git metadata does not own `/tmp/trivela-review-frontend`; the two `git worktree list` outputs are separate.  
Reproduction: Compare worktree lists from the two repositories.  
Impact: The documented frontend cleanup fails, leaving its worktree registered. It fails safely, but the promised complete cleanup is inaccurate.  
Recommended correction: Run removal from the repository that owns the specific worktree.

### Finding 8

Title: Frontend decision-safety test coverage is overstated  
Severity: LOW  
Status: CONFIRMED  
Repository: Frontend  
File / lines: [AGENTS.md:38–50](/tmp/trivela-review-frontend/AGENTS.md:38), [decision-safety.spec.ts:7](/tmp/trivela-review-frontend/e2e/decision-safety.spec.ts:7), [contract-deterministic.spec.ts:82](/tmp/trivela-review-frontend/e2e/contract-deterministic.spec.ts:82)  
Evidence: `decision-safety.spec.ts` covers shadow framing and a bare `TAKE`. The empty-state invariant is in another spec, and there is no dedicated assertion preventing statistically insignificant point estimates from being described as established edges.  
Reproduction: Compare the four policy bullets with assertions in the named test.  
Impact: The documentation gives stronger assurance than the named guard provides.  
Recommended correction: Name the actual enforcing specs and add or explicitly disclaim the missing statistical-language assertion.

## 6. Speculative risks

### Risk 1

Title: Non-default Vercel pushes are assumed harmless without dashboard evidence  
Severity: MEDIUM  
Status: SPECULATIVE  
Repository: Backend and frontend  
File / lines: [backend AGENTS.md:98–107](/tmp/trivela-review-backend/AGENTS.md:98), [frontend AGENTS.md:25–36](/tmp/trivela-review-frontend/AGENTS.md:25)  
Evidence: No `vercel.json` exists; production-branch selection is dashboard-side and was not locally verifiable.  
Impact: If Vercel’s configured production branch differs from the Git default branch, a supposedly preview-only push could affect production.  
Recommended correction: Require Son to confirm and record the configured Vercel production branch before the first feature-branch push.

### Risk 2

Title: Read-only is not a confidentiality boundary  
Severity: MEDIUM  
Status: SPECULATIVE  
Repository: Backend  
File / lines: [codex-review.md:9–18](/tmp/trivela-review-backend/agent-prompts/codex-review.md:9)  
Evidence: `-C` sets the working directory but does not scope reads. This reviewer could read the main checkout, frontend repository, developer-local virtualenv, and application installation outside the review worktree. No secret was read or found in the diff.  
Impact: An erroneous or adversarial instruction could cause unrelated host files to be inspected or printed even though writes remain blocked.  
Recommended correction: Run reviews from a sanitized checkout/account/container and document that `--sandbox read-only` protects integrity, not confidentiality.

`preview_start` behavior and actual Railway/Vercel dashboard settings remain `UNVERIFIED_ENVIRONMENT_DEPENDENT`.

## 7. Optional improvements

- Remove the frontend EOF whitespace reported by `git diff --check`.
- Move the explicit “no temporal or target leakage” rule from the reviewer checklist into the canonical hard invariants.
- Reword “components only ever render client-side”: the components do SSR-render their initial states; only fetched data becomes available after `useEffect`.

## 8. WC26 reference classification

- `LEGITIMATE_ARCHIVE`: the fail-closed World Cup archive plane and archived evidence references.
- `LEGITIMATE_HISTORICAL_DOCUMENTATION`: instructions preserving old paths in V7–V9.5.
- `BACKWARD_COMPATIBILITY`: the existing `/bet-suggester` route/name.
- `STALE_PATH_OR_NAME`: the active reviewer path `backend/research_archive/...`.
- No new `ACTIVE_TRIVELA_ASSUMPTION` was introduced.
- The archived WC26 project, archive-plane code/data, and V7–V9 historical documents were untouched.

## 9. Multi-league risk assessment

The workflow correctly identifies Trivela as active and multi-league, distinguishes league from tournament assumptions, requires stable identity and IANA-zone scrutiny, and preserves evidence classes and explicit fallbacks.

No modelling or league implementation changed, so this review does not establish that existing code is free of multi-league or leakage defects. The reviewer prompt includes temporal/target-leakage review, but that rule should also live in the shared contract.

## 10. Security and deployment assessment

- Secret scan: no key, token, private-key, `.env`, database, binary, virtualenv, `node_modules`, corpus, or log artifacts added.
- Absolute developer paths occur only in agent workflow documentation, not runtime code.
- Railway/Vercel configuration, Dockerfiles, startup commands, CI, environment schemas, APIs, migrations, and models are unchanged.
- `REAL_MONEY_SIGNALS_ENABLED=false` remains in `.env.example`; configuration still defaults false; the diff introduces no enabling path.
- No push, merge, deploy, migration, production write, approval activation, or corpus publication was performed.
- Production-safety is nevertheless blocked by the default Playwright target and ambiguous push prompt.

## 11. Role-separation assessment

This part is strong:

- Implementer and reviewer responsibilities are explicit.
- Reviewer is read-only and owns no implementation.
- Findings must be reproduced independently before application.
- Disagreements must be surfaced to Son.
- Detached fixed-commit worktrees prevent branch drift.
- Backend and frontend are handled as separate repositories.

No implementer response exists yet, so there is no disagreement to adjudicate.

## 12. Prioritised correction list

P0:

1. Inject complete, immutable review inputs into the launch.
   - Minimum acceptance: a generated prompt contains both full ranges, no `<REPO>`/`<BASE_COMMIT>`/`<CLAUDE_COMMIT>` placeholders, and the launched reviewer independently verifies both ancestries.

2. Make independent validation executable without permitting source mutation.
   - Minimum acceptance: under the documented reviewer launch, backend pytest and frontend typecheck/build can complete using disposable writable scratch space, followed by clean `git status --short` in both worktrees.

3. Make default Playwright validation hermetic and non-production.
   - Minimum acceptance: the default command makes zero requests to the production hostname; live smoke tests require an explicit opt-in and operator approval.

4. Remove the push contradiction.
   - Minimum acceptance: one unambiguous rule remains; a local-reviewer scenario requires no push, while a cloud-reviewer scenario requires Son’s deployment-branch confirmation before any branch push.

P1:

1. Correct the remediation-record path.
   - Minimum acceptance: every mandatory preread command succeeds exactly as written from the documented backend working directory.

2. Correct the virtualenv description and provide fresh-checkout setup.
   - Minimum acceptance: the documented procedure produces a usable interpreter in a clean checkout where `.venv` is initially absent.

3. Make cleanup repository-aware.
   - Minimum acceptance: disposable backend and frontend review worktrees can each be removed from their owning repository without affecting the implementation worktrees.

4. Verify Vercel’s production branch before regular branch pushes.
   - Minimum acceptance: the handoff records Son-confirmed dashboard state and the exact branch classified as production.

P2:

- Correct the decision-safety test attribution or add the missing assertion.
- Remove frontend EOF whitespace.
- Promote temporal/target-leakage language into the canonical contract.
- Clarify SSR/useEffect wording.

## 13. Adoption decision

Role separation, Git isolation, MCP fallback direction, WC26 preservation, multi-league framing, real-money safety, and the absence of runtime changes are all sound. Adoption is conditional on fixing the four P0 issues; P1 corrections should land before regular use.

`READY_AFTER_P0_CORRECTIONS`
